correctness.rationale: A direct commutator argument establishes center preservation, then the identity forces quotient-linearity. Comparing the central cocycle and antisymmetrizing yields the equivalent condition omega((T-cI)v,(T-cI)w)=c(c+1)omega(v,w). The remaining symmetric cocycle is exactly the polarization of -c omega(Tv,v)/2, hence leaves an arbitrary linear functional. Nonzero multipliers are symplectic-similitude torsors; zero multiplier matrices have totally isotropic image, with rank-r maps counted by surjections onto the explicitly enumerated isotropic r-spaces. Integer formulas and sampled group-identity checks passed; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.
